sources.entry: Gatus | Health dashboard and uptime monitor configured in YAML

summary.one_liner: Gatus is a self-hosted, YAML-configured health dashboard and uptime monitor that checks HTTP, ICMP, TCP and DNS endpoints against conditions and sends alerts.
summary.what_it_does: Gatus monitors services over HTTP, ICMP, TCP, DNS, SSH, and other protocols listed in its FAQ, running checks on a configurable interval. Each endpoint is evaluated against a list of conditions on values such as status code, response time, certificate expiration, body (with JSONPath), and IP address. Failed conditions mark an endpoint unhealthy, and alerts can be triggered after a failure threshold is reached. Alerts are sent through many providers, including Slack, Teams, PagerDuty, Discord, Twilio, and others listed in the README. The README also describes suites for chaining multi-step workflows, external endpoints that receive pushed status results, SSH tunneling, and a dashboard with badges, metrics, and an API. Configuration is loaded from YAML files, with optional SQLite or PostgreSQL storage and in-memory storage by default.
use_cases: monitor web services and APIs for uptime
alert on-call via Slack, PagerDuty or Discord when a service fails
check TLS certificate expiration and domain expiry
run automated user acceptance or multi-step API tests
display a public or internal status dashboard for services
monitor services behind a private network via pushed status results
stack: Kubernetes (Helm chart, as mentioned by the author)
notable: Conditions on response time, body, certificate expiry and IP address, not just status codes
Suites for chaining endpoints in a shared context, marked ALPHA
External endpoints let an agent in a private network push health results
Alerting to many providers including Slack, PagerDuty, Discord, Teams and Twilio
Config directory merging and environment variable substitution
caveats: Suites are marked ALPHA and suite-level alerts are not supported yet
Tunneling may add latency and skew response-time measurements
Default in-memory storage does not persist data across restarts
keywords: keep an eye on my websites
get notified when my server goes down
